title: Feedback wanted on my mobile RPG: train skills, fight monsters and rebuild a forgotten village
author: NoMacJustMagic
selftext:
I'm a solo dev working on a mobile RPG set in a forgotten valley.

What you do:

\- Train 14 skills like woodcutting, mining, herbalism and smithing

\- Fight monsters and unlock new attack techniques as you level

\- Take quests from the villagers and explore the valley

\- Rebuild the old village of Hazelbrink by upgrading its buildings

\- Online multiplayer with trading and groups is planned

The 3D models are made with Tripo from my own designs, the animations come from Mixamo, and everything runs in three.js.

I'd love honest feedback:

\- What do you think of the visuals? Does the style feel consistent?

\- Does it look like something you'd want to play?

\- What stands out as the weakest part?

comments.author: Opening_Wafer_6584
comments.body:
Hey, Alex here from Tripo. The style feels pretty cohesive from what you’ve shown, especially considering the models are being generated individually from your own designs.

Tripo → Mixamo → three.js is also a nice lightweight pipeline for a solo mobile project.

I’d be curious which asset types have been easiest to keep visually consistent so far, and which ones have required the most iteration.

replies.author: NoMacJustMagic
replies.body:
Thanks Alex, means a lot!

Easiest so far: buildings and props. With a clear concept image and "Remove Lighting" on they come out very close to the style I want and the village feels like one place.

Most iteration: characters and creatures. Faces and proportions drift between generations and since the models come without a skeleton I rig them myself and use Mixamo for the animations, which takes a few tries before the walk and attack look right.

comments.author: markhobsie
comments.body: Reminds me alot of classic WoW (which is a good thing imo!) and it looks like there's already a lot to do? Atm i'd say the overall image still looks quite flat, there's no ambient occlusion and the ambient lighting is overly bright. I think self shadowing and tweaks to those things would really help make it feel more solid, but the general style I fond of!

replies.author: NoMacJustMagic
replies.body:
Thanks, that's a big compliment! Classic WoW is definitely a big inspiration.

And you're right about the lighting, it still looks too flat. I've been keeping it light for mobile performance, but I'll try some ambient occlusion, toning down the ambient light and adding self-shadowing. Appreciate the concrete tips!
